patch.value: Two governance loosenings sit in the committed assurance registry with no entry in the append-only workspace audit stream, which freezes every future audited write and is invisible to both validate and health

The audited workspace stream replays to exactly the on-disk state of every workspace singleton it governs, verified by a check that compares replay against disk rather than only verifying the hash chain; The two divergent assertions are reconciled by a recorded mutation that states which value is intended and why, never by editing either file to match the other; pm validate and pm health both report singleton-replay divergence, so a committed divergence fails CI at the commit that introduces it instead of freezing the next writer; A direct edit to a workspace singleton that bypasses the audited mutation path is refused or reported at the point the change is committed, with a negative control proving detection; The loosening-authorization guard is proven to classify a tightening as a tightening, with a negative control for each bound polarity, so an earned stricter bound never requires the authorization a weaker one does; Assurance registry writes are restorable to any recorded version, demonstrated by restoring the registry to a prior state and replaying forward
The audited stream for a workspace singleton always reproduces the singleton, and any divergence is reported by an integrity surface before it blocks a write
The append-only workspace stream is the proof that a governance bound was never weakened silently. Two bounds were weakened silently, so for the assurance registry the proof does not currently hold.

The assurance registry is unmutatable through its own audited path: every pm assurance put fails with a state conflict, so no bound can be tightened, no gate promoted, and no earned ratchet locked in.

The divergence is reconciled by a recorded entry, the two loosenings are either re-authorized or reverted on the record, and an integrity check reports singleton-replay divergence so it can never again be discovered only by attempting a write.
Discovered by attempting a legitimate tightening this session; the registry has been frozen since 2026-08-13 and neither of the two standing integrity surfaces reports anything wrong.

message: File the assurance registry audit divergence found by attempting an earned ratchet tightening

author: harness:claude-code

patch.value:
## How it was found

Attempted a legitimate tightening: three graph-finding ceilings had been earned down to zero by this session's hygiene batch (`legacy_duplicate_edge` 8 to 0, `legacy_no_blocker_sentinel` 98 to 0, `missing_reference_terminal` 3 to 0), so their declared ceilings of 8, 98 and 3 were now over-permissive and should become real regression gates at 0.

`pm assurance put assertion ...` refused:

```
Workspace history state for "assurance.json" changed outside the audited mutation path.
code: workspace_history_state_conflict
reason: out_of_band_workspace_state
```

The refusal is correct. The state it describes is real, and it predates this session.

## The divergence, measured by replay

Both `.agents/pm/assurance.json` and `.agents/pm/history/_workspace.jsonl` are unmodified in the working tree. Both were last written by commit `0132ed74b` ("Native assurance and structural outcome graph governance", PR #992). So the divergence is committed state and reproduces from a clean checkout.

Replaying all 167 workspace entries (1,240 patch operations) to reconstruct `metadata.documents["assurance.json"]` and comparing order-insensitively against the on-disk registry:

- `version`: same
- `measurements`: same (all 40)
- `gates`: same (all 3)
- `assertions`: **differs in exactly two of forty**

```
health-telemetry-zero
  enforcement:            audited "block"   on disk "warn"
  authorization_decision: audited absent    on disk "pm-jezo"

graph-outcome-reachable-floor
  floor:                  audited 2438      on disk 2434
  negative_control:       audited 2438 pass / 2437 fail
                          on disk 2434 pass / 2433 fail
```

Both differences are loosenings. A `block` to `warn` downgrade is a loosening of enforcement; a floor moved from 2438 down to 2434 is a loosening of the bound. These are exactly the two edit shapes the `authorization_decision` requirement and the append-only stream exist to make undeniable, and neither has an entry.

`health-telemetry-zero` at least names its authorization: pm-jezo is a real closed ADR, "Health checks are advisory vs blocking: telemetry_* never flips ok:false", so the decision was legitimate and only the recording is missing. `graph-outcome-reachable-floor` carries no `authorization_decision` on disk at all, so its four-point loosening has neither an entry nor a stated authority.

## Why the hash chain does not catch it

`pm history _workspace --verify` reports `ok: true`, 167 entries, zero errors, and a valid `latest_after_hash`. That is correct and not contradictory: the chain proves every recorded entry follows from the previous one. It cannot prove that the recorded entries account for every change to the document, because a change made without an entry leaves the chain internally consistent and simply shorter than the truth.

Chain integrity and state agreement are different properties. Only the second one was violated, and only the second one is unchecked.

## Why the two standing integrity surfaces miss it

- `pm validate --check-history-drift` reports `status: ok`, `missing_streams: 0`, `unreadable_streams: 0`, `hash_mismatches: 0`, `chain_mismatches: 0` across 2,455 checked items. It walks item streams. The workspace singleton is not an item, so it is out of scope.
- `pm health --check-only` reports `ok: true` with no failing checks.

So the only thing in the system that detects this is the mutation guard, which by construction reports it to the next writer rather than to CI. The divergence was committed, released in v2026.8.13, and surfaced for the first time when someone tried to tighten a ratchet.

## Consequence right now

The registry is frozen. A no-op re-put of an unchanged definition fails with the same conflict, so this is not specific to the values being written. That means for as long as the divergence stands:

- no earned ceiling can be tightened, so cleanup cannot be locked in;
- no gate can be promoted from warn to block;
- no new measurement or assertion can be declared.

The three ceilings this session earned to zero remain declared at 8, 98 and 3, which is why a regression re-introducing sentinels or duplicate spellings would still pass CI.

## Boundary

Do not reconcile by editing either file to match the other. Editing the singleton to match the stream would silently revert two decisions, one of which is legitimately authorized by pm-jezo. Editing the stream would forge an append-only record, which is the exact harm. The reconciliation must be a recorded mutation that states the intended value and its authority, which is the same shape pm-9j2r3b established for unrecorded merge results.

message: Record the replay diff, the reproduction, and why the two standing integrity surfaces miss it
